figures.title: Convergence: columns and sample paths
figures.caption: In probability: each fixed tolerance is exceeded with probability tending to zero. Almost surely: almost every whole path eventually stays within each fixed tolerance. A finite grid illustrates the quantifiers; it does not prove a limit.

figures.title: Normal errors at three scales
figures.caption: The same horizontal and vertical scales show narrowing, unit-scale, and wider Normal distributions. The complete limit calculations remain in this solution; finite curves alone do not specify a sequence.

figures.title: Tail events ignore a finite beginning
figures.caption: For the limiting-average event in the text, a finite deleted sum divided by n tends to zero. The limiting question is unchanged.

figures.title: Comparing the empirical and population CDFs
figures.caption: Solid: empirical CDF for ten synthetic observations. Dashed: population CDF. The largest vertical discrepancy uses both sides of every jump, including for the discrete example. One finite sample illustrates the comparison, not convergence.

figures.title: Uniform error and a separated minimum
figures.caption: Outside |θ| < 0.8 the population gap is at least 0.64. Two errors of size 0.1 leave a positive gap. This is the comparison in the proof; an approximate minimizer also requires its optimization error to vanish.
